title: Bonus: How the Pharmacy Boards Work

questions.stem: Is the pharmacy board exam adaptive, like the nursing boards?

options.text: Yes, it stops early when the computer is sure
No, it is a fixed form; everyone answers all questions
It is adaptive only in the second half

questions.explanation: B is correct: the pharmacy board exam is a fixed form, and everyone answers all 225 questions. A describes an adaptive exam. C and D are not how the exam works.

questions.stem: How many questions and how much time does the pharmacy board exam have?
questions.explanation: D is correct: 225 questions in 6 hours. A and C do not match the published format. B is a variable-length range, but the pharmacy board exam is a fixed 225 questions.

questions.stem: About how long is there for each question?
questions.explanation: B is correct: 360 minutes divided by 225 questions is 1.6 minutes, about one and a half minutes each. A is far too short. C and D are far too long for 225 questions in 6 hours.

questions.stem: Which statement about exam attempts is correct?

options.text: 5 attempts total, with no more than 3 in a 12-month period

questions.explanation: D is correct: candidates are allowed 5 attempts, and the bulletin limits attempts to 3 in a 12-month period. A is wrong because attempts are limited. C and B do not match the published limits.

questions.stem: How are pharmacy board results reported?
questions.explanation: C is correct: results are pass or fail. A, B, and D are not how results are reported.

questions.stem: Which statement about the law exam is correct?

options.text: It is separate and focuses on your state's pharmacy law
It is part of the clinical board exam
It is national with no state content

questions.explanation: A is correct: the law exam is separate from the clinical board exam and focuses on your state's pharmacy law; your state board decides which law exam you take. B is wrong because it is a separate exam. C describes the clinical board exam. D describes part of the clinical board exam's content.

questions.stem: Which exam-day steps are recommended? Select all that apply.

options.text: Make sure your identification matches your registration name
Bring study notes to review during breaks inside the exam
Use the optional breaks to reset
Write units on every calculation step

questions.explanation: A, C, D, and E are correct: matching identification, arriving early, using the optional breaks, and writing units on every calculation step. B is wrong because study notes and other study materials are not allowed in the exam, including during breaks.

questions.stem: One hard calculation has taken 10 minutes. What is the best strategy?

options.text: Keep working until it is solved
Make your best answer and keep moving
Skip it and come back at the end

questions.explanation: B is correct: don't let one hard calculation eat 10 minutes; make your best answer and keep moving. A uses up time needed for later questions. C is wrong because the exam does not let you skip a question and come back to it later. D wastes the chance to earn the point.

questions.stem: A candidate answers questions well early on. Will the exam stop early?

options.text: Yes, once a passing score is reached
No, it does not stop early

questions.explanation: C is correct: the exam does not stop early; everyone answers all 225 questions. A and B describe an adaptive exam. D is wrong because finishing early is not about running out of time.

questions.stem: Which statements about the pharmacy board exam format are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, C, and E are correct: 225 questions, 6 hours, a fixed form, and pass or fail results. D is wrong because the exam is not adaptive. F is wrong because results are pass or fail, not a percentile.
